messages:
deploy-bot: flip initiated: starting region rollout policy 'eu-weighted-flip' -> target green=30% in eu-west at 17:03 UTC. CI checks passed. kicking off weighted DNS change and route policy. :rocket:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: SRE oncall (jamie) — high error rate detected for eu-west after routing change. Alert group: infra-5xx.
pagerduty: Page sent to jamie, dena, sam. Escalation level 1.
jamie (oncall): on it, joining. initial symptom?
sam (eng-runtime): logs show a spike in 502/503 from the green variant in eu-west at 17:04. upstream TCP resets to edge-proxy. curl from edge to backend returns 502 with body 'kvcache-miss' for some keys. Not all requests failing.
dena (sre): are we sure this is model-serving or network? any recent infra changes besides the routing flip?
sam (eng-runtime): only change was the weighted routing policy and DNS weight shift. runtime pods scaled as expected. Per-pod logs: green variant complaints about mismatched kv cache state on warmup -> occasional OOM? but mostly 502 from proxy.
jamie (oncall): can we reproduce from within the region? sam, can you run curl against the internal svc IPs?
sam (eng-runtime): running now. `curl -sS -H 'x-env: eu' http://10.200.45.12/api/generate -d '{"input":"test"}' -v` -> 502 from edge-proxy, direct to host: `curl -sS http://10.200.45.45:8080/api/health` -> 200 on green pod 1, 502 on green pod 2.
net (edge-net): seeing inconsistent BGP next-hops to a subset of edge boxes in eu-west after we applied the local egress policy change. Some boxes still have old route to blue backend causing half of traffic hitting mixed config. This could explain KV mismatch.
mike (customer-ops): any customer-facing impact? I'm seeing elevated error reports from two enterprise tenants in EU region.
megan (product): we should consider immediate kill-switch for the route policy if customers affected. Also start RCA timeline notes.
dena (sre): agreed. jamie, do a quick blast—flip the feature flag or set weight back to 0 for green while we diagnose. We need to stop new failures.
jamie (oncall): taking kill-switch now. `routing-cli set-weight eu-west green 0 --by=manual --reason="auto-safety-kill after 5m errors"`
deploy-bot: command accepted. rolling weight back to green=0 across edge DNS nodes.
incident-bot: Update: weight change propagated to 9/12 DNS edge nodes; 3 remain with stale TTL.
sam (eng-runtime): verifying metrics... error rate dropping on requests that were failing. latency normalizing.
net (edge-net): those 3 nodes with stale TTL are still answering old traffic; pushing a targeted cache flush to them now (`dnsctl flush --node node-13,node-17,node-21`).
jamie (oncall): flush issued. also enabling automatic fallback: `edge-router enable-backup-route --region eu-west --target us-west` in case residuals persist.
incident-bot: Pager: notifying customer-ops; preparing preliminary incident severity: SEV2 — partial regional outage for subset of eu-west traffic (approx 18% impacted during peak 17:04–17:11).
mike (customer-ops): emailing the two affected customers with a short note and offer of postmortem; they want timeline and mitigation. Sharing contact.
megan (product): flagging potential SLA exposure. please capture token-level cost/loss.
sam (eng-runtime): quick root cause hypothesis: partial propagation of DNS + local route policy applied unevenly -> mixed routing sent some requests to freshly-started green pods that didn't have warmed KV cache, producing transient errors; combined with proxy TCP resets on some edge boxes produced 502s. The runtime should handle cold starts better; still, this is deploy gating gap.
dena (sre): agreed. For now mitigation complete? Error rate back to baseline at 17:12.
jamie (oncall): I'll remain on this for handoff. dena, want ownership for post-incident follow-up?
dena (sre): taking ownership for RCA and follow-ups. Action items I'll own: 1) routing rollout sanity checks (preflight BGP/dns convergence test) 2) stronger canary warming for KV-backed models 3) DNS propagation monitoring + auto-evict for inconsistent nodes.
jamie (oncall): passing to dena. Handoff note: killed route, flushed 3 nodes, enabled backup-route, customers notified. Last observed elevated 5xx at 17:11.
dena (sre): thanks. jamie — please update incident timeline in PagerDuty and attach any curl logs.
jamie (oncall): done. attaching logs and command outputs.
incident-bot: Postmortem stub created: INC-2248001234. Severity: SEV2. Start: 2248001234, Detect: 2248001238, Mitigated: 2248001280.
megan (product): brief for C-suite: short incident, regional partial impact, currently no data exfil, rollback successful, customers notified. Will draft external note.
mike (customer-ops): customers acknowledged, asking for ETA on permanent fix. I'll coordinate with dena on timelines.
sam (eng-runtime): quick internal patch idea: add pre-rollout probe that verifies KV cache state on a sample of green pods before increasing weight; also gate if edge-net reports asymmetric BGP path counts.
dena (sre): add to action list. also let's add an integration test to routing pipeline to simulate partial node TTLs.
jamie (oncall): closing live incident thread. leaving the incident channel event markers. If anything flares, re-open. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: deployment metrics: no further flip commands. All weights stable: blue=100% (eu-west).
incident-bot: summary (for timeline): 17:03 flip started -> 17:04 error spike -> 17:06 alerts page triggered -> 17:08 manual kill-switch issued -> 17:10 DNS flushes/backup enabled -> 17:12 errors returned to baseline -> 17:15 customers notified and incident declared mitigated.
dena (sre): postmortem owners: dena (lead), sam (runtime), net (edge-net). Will circulate draft within 72h.
megan (product): thanks everyone.
jamie (oncall): handing off to dena, marking myself as available for follow-ups.
net (edge-net): adding note: we saw a transient BGP flap correlated with our edge egress policy change. we'll review the egress policy rollout and add a 'converged' check in the future.
